name: Bhaskara Rao Bollineni
forbes_bio: Cardiothoracic surgeon Bhaskara Rao Bollineni founded KIMS Hospitals in 2000 with a 200-bed hospital in his home town of Nellore in southern India.
The company owns and operates 25 hospitals with a total of 8,300 beds across the states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Kerala.
The older of his two sons, Abhinay, who's also a doctor, is chief executive while the younger son Adwik is has a board seat.
Its flagship hospital in the southern city of Secundraabad has 1,000 beds.
Bollineni has performed more than 30,000 surgeries over a career spanning nearly three decades.

name: Huh Jae-myung
forbes_bio: Huh Jae-myung is the largest shareholder of Iljin Materials, a manufacturer of electric foils used in consumer electronic products, and lithium batteries. He stepped down as CEO in 2021.
The firm is a subsidiary of the Iljin group, a conglomerate with interests in electric machinery, steel, construction, medical equipment and media.
He is the second son of Iljin group's founder and chairman Huh Jin-kyu, who started the company as a metal maker in Seoul in 1968.
He is married to Eun-hye Park of Kumho Asiana, a conglomerate with primary interests in transportation.

name: Joseph Baratta
forbes_bio: Joseph Baratta has served as Blackstone's global head of private equity since 2012.
He joined the alternative asset management giant in 1998 and moved to London in 2001 to help build the firm's European private equity business.
Baratta serves on the boards of a number of Blackstone portfolio companies including Ancestry.com, Medline and Merlin Entertainments Group.
Before joining Blackstone, Baratta worked for investment firms Tinicum Incorporated and McCown De Leeuw & Company and in the M&A department of Morgan Stanley.
He graduated magna cum laude from Georgetown University and is a former member of the school's Board of Trustees.

name: Valery Kustov
forbes_bio: Valery Kustov is the founder of EFKO, one of the largest Russian food companies with annual sales about $4 billion.

Kustov, along with partners, took control of a small perfume and essential oil producer during privatization in Russia in the 1990s, later rebranding the business to produce sunflower oil and mayonnaise.
EFKO now produces industrial fats, egg products, sunflower oil, sauces, soap and biotechnology products like sweet proteins.
In 2025 EFKO bought former oil-seed assets of US food company Bunge in Russia.

name: Zhang Cheng Fei
forbes_bio: Zhang Cheng Fei is the deputy CEO of Nine Dragons Paper of China, one of Asia's largest paper and packaging companies.
Zhang's sister Cheung Yan, who chairs Nine Dragons, is also a billionaire.
Zhang's brother-in-law Liu Ming Chung, the CEO of Nine Dragons, is also one of three billionaires in the family.

name: Harry Klagsbrun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2024); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Harry Klagsbrun joined publicly traded Swedish private equity firm EQT AB in 2006.
EQT has roughly $83 billion in assets under management.
EQT primarily invests in private equity but has also put funds into venture capital, real estate and infrastructure.
Klagsbrun joined the board of publicly traded Securitas AB in 2021.
Klagsbrun, whose father was a clothing designer, got his MBA from NYU as a Fulbright scholar before joining Smith Barney.

name: Roy Vagelos
forbes_bio: Roy Vagelos served as the chairman and chief executive officer of Merck & Co. from 1984 to 1994.
Vagelos graduated from the University of Pennsylvania in 1950 and earned an M.D. at Columbia University in 1954.
He joined Regeneron Pharmaceuticals as chairman in 1995 and led the company for nearly 29 years.
He also served as chairman of Theravance, a pharmaceutical company he cofounded in 1996.
Vagelos has authored over 100 scientific papers and is an elected member of the National Academy of Sciences.
forbes_facts: Vagelos and his wife Diana have donated hundreds of millions of dollars to Columbia University's medical school.

name: Vlad Vendrow
forbes_bio: Vlad Vendrow is a cofounder and Chief Technology Officer of RingCentral, a cloud-based business communications provider.
The company went public in 2013 on the New York Stock Exchange, and has customers more than 100 countries.
RingCentral reached $1 billion in sales for the first time in 2020.
Before founding the company, Vendrow was the director of engineering at Motorola and Ring Zero Systems, a software provider.
Vendrow is the author of more than 40 software-related patents.

name: Chris Pavlovski
forbes_bio: Chris Pavlovski founded Rumble, a video platform popular on the political right, in 2013 and currently serves as its CEO.
The company's first big outside investor was Narya, a venture capital firm cofounded by JD Vance and supported by Peter Thiel.
Rumble went public via a SPAC deal in 2022 that was managed by Howard Lutnick, Donald Trump's pick for commerce secretary.
Today, popular content creators on Rumble include Donald Trump Jr., Dan Bongino, Russell Brand and Steve Bannon.
A $775 million investment from cryptocurrency giant Tether in December 2024 pushed Pavlovski's controlling stake in Rumble over $1 billion.
Pavlovski also founded Cosmic Development, an IT outsourcing firm with over 250 employees and offices in North Macedonia and Serbia.
forbes_facts: Pavlovski has been building websites since he was a teenager.
Pavlovski's parents are Macedonian immigrants, and he was born in Toronto.
